newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Tanzania says Burundi trade ban stays.
newsitem.headline: Tanzania says Burundi trade ban stays.

text.p: Tanzanian Foreign Minister Jakaya Kikwete has said African states would not end economic sanctions imposed on Burundi despite military leader Pierre Buyoya's decision to lift the ban on political parties.
Local newspapers on Sunday quoted Kikwete as saying the sanctions, agreed by neighbouring African states at a meeting in Arusha, northern Tanzania, on July 31, would remain in force.
"A return to full parliamentary and constitutional rule is a fundamental requirement for lifting the sanctions," he was quoted as telling reporters in Dar es Salaam on Saturday.
"We (the neighbouring states) also want to see direct negotiations with other political groups on power-sharing."
Buyoya issued a decree in Bujumbura on Friday restoring the national assembly and dropping a ban on political parties imposed after he seized power in an army coup on July 25.
But he made it clear that Burundi's constitution remained suspended and demonstrations were still banned.
Opposition groups outside Burundi received the statement with scepticism, describing the changes as "cosmetic".
